mainTopic: The end of the math for רבי יוחנן's round סוכה, the potters' booths and מזוזה, and the two ברייתות (גנב״ך and רקב״ש) that a סוכה is כשרה no matter who built it, if its roof gives shade
overview: This amud opens by finishing a calculation from the previous amud about how big a round סוכה must be, according to רבי יוחנן. The גמרא then notes that the math overestimates the real size. Next, רבי לוי in the name of רבי מאיר teaches about two potters' booths, one inside the other. The inner one is a year-round home, so it needs a מזוזה but is not a valid סוכה. The outer one is a valid סוכה and needs no מזוזה. The outer booth is not treated as a gatehouse because the booths are not permanent. Two ברייתות, remembered as גנב״ך and רקב״ש, teach that booths built by or for גוים, women, animals, כותים, shepherds, fig-driers, and guards are all כשרה. רב חסדא explains that the roof must be made for shade, and each ברייתא's 'any kind' includes the other list. The גמרא explains that one תנא names the permanent booths outright, while the other names outright the booths whose builders are obligated in the מצוה.

steps.title: A circle around a square is half again the square's perimeter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its geometry rule: a circle drawn around a square has a circumference equal to the square's perimeter plus half of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A square that fits inside a circle: the circle is bigger by half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a math rule it began on the previous amud. The rule explains how big a round סוכה must be to hold a square of the required size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A kosher סוכה must be able to hold a square of a certain size. If you draw a circle around that square, this rule says the circle is the square's perimeter plus half again. So a square with a 16 אמות perimeter needs a circle of 24 אמות, which matches רבי יוחנן's number.

keyTerms.meaning: that comes out from inside (here: a square that fits inside the circle)

steps.confusionAlert: This line continues a calculation that started on the previous amud. It is not a fresh topic. It completes the support for רבי יוחנן's measurement of a round סוכה.

phrases.english: A square that fits inside a circle: (the circle is larger by) half.
phrases.notes: In other words, the circumference of the surrounding circle equals the square's perimeter plus half of that perimeter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the geometric explanation, begun on the previous amud, for רבי יוחנן's measurement of a round סוכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The circle around a square has a circumference of the square's perimeter plus half (a 1.5 ratio).

steps.title: Real-world observation: the circle is not that much bigger
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this rule is not exact. When you actually look, the circle is not as big as the rule says.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so, because we see that it is not that much.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the 'half again' rule is not accurate. Looking at a real circle around a square shows a smaller difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In reality, a square with a 16 אמות perimeter has a surrounding circle of only about 17.8 אמות, not 24. So the rule overshoots. The גמרא admits the number is bigger than the true measurement, which means רבי יוחנן's figure is stricter than strictly necessary.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'half again' rule for a circle around a square is an overestimate, and the גמרא itself says so based on what we can see.

phrases.english: But it is not so,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא קָחָזֵינַן דְּלָא הָוֵי כּוּלֵּי הַאי.
phrases.english: for we see that it is not that much.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies the geometric rule from step 1 using direct observation.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The accuracy of the 'half again' ratio, not the overall law of a round סוכה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Observation shows the real circumference is smaller than perimeter plus half.

steps.title: Two potters' booths, one inside the other
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי, quoting רבי מאיר, rules on two potters' booths. The inner one is not a valid סוכה but needs a מזוזה. The outer one is a valid סוכה and does not need a מזוזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי said in the name of רבי מאיר: two potters' booths, one inside the other. The inner one is not a סוכה and is obligated in מזוזה. The outer one is a סוכה and is exempt from מזוזה.
steps.whatsHappening: A brand-new teaching begins. It is about potters who have two booths, one inside the other, and whether each counts as a סוכה and whether each needs a מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The potter lives in the inner booth all year. That makes it a real home, so it needs a מזוזה. But because he lives there anyway, sitting there on סוכות does not show he is doing it for the מצוה, so it is not a valid סוכה. The outer booth is only a work and selling area. It is not a home, so it needs no מזוזה, and sitting in it on סוכות clearly shows it is for the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: the parchment scroll fixed on the doorpost of a dwelling

steps.whyThisMatters: The case shows that a place that is a year-round home works opposite ways for the two מצוות. Being a fixed home creates the מזוזה obligation, but it ruins the סוכה, which must be noticeably for the festival.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Levi said in the name of Rabbi Meir:
Two booths of potters,
one inside the other:
the inner one is not a (valid) sukkah,
phrases.notes: He lives there all year, so it is not evident that he is sitting there for the מצוה.

phrases.english: and it is obligated in mezuzah.
And the outer one is a (valid) sukkah,
and it is exempt from mezuzah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic. It moves from measuring a round סוכה to the status of craftsmen's booths.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The inner potters' booth is not a valid סוכה and needs a מזוזה. The outer booth is a valid סוכה and is exempt from מזוזה.

steps.title: Why isn't the outer booth like a gatehouse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the exemption: the outer booth leads into the inner home, so it should count as its gatehouse and need a מזוזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why? Let the outer one be like a gatehouse of the inner one, and be obligated in מזוזה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the second half of רבי מאיר's ruling, that the outer booth is exempt from מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gatehouse that leads into a home needs a מזוזה, even though nobody lives in the gatehouse itself. Here, the outer booth is the entrance to the inner home. So by that logic it should need a מזוזה too.

keyTerms.meaning: a gatehouse (entrance room leading into a home)

phrases.english: And why (is the outer one exempt)?
Let the outer one be like a gatehouse of the inner one,
and let it be obligated in mezuzah!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? תִּהְוֵי חִיצוֹנָה כְּבֵית שַׁעַר הַפְּנִימִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the מזוזה exemption of the outer booth from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the outer booth is exempt from מזוזה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A gatehouse leading into a home needs a מזוזה. The outer booth leads into the inner home, so it should need one too.

steps.title: Because it is not permanent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the booths are not truly permanent structures, so the gatehouse rule does not apply.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in one short phrase: the structure is not permanent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gatehouse rule applies to an entrance into a fixed, permanent home. According to the Sefaria explanation, even the inner booth is not a full permanent house. It needs its own מזוזה because he lives there, but it is not strong enough to make its entrance a gatehouse that is obligated. So the outer booth stays exempt.
steps.whatToRemember: The outer potter's booth is a valid סוכה and exempt from מזוזה. It is not treated as a gatehouse because the booths are not permanent structures.

phrases.english: Because it is not permanent.
phrases.notes: The Sefaria explanation is that even the inner booth is not a full permanent residence. Others read it as referring to the outer booth itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the gatehouse challenge from step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the gatehouse rule requires a permanent structure.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The outer booth leads into a home, so it should need a מזוזה like any gatehouse.
steps.terutzMaskana: The booth is not permanent, so it does not become an obligated gatehouse, and the outer booth stays exempt.

steps.title: A סוכה is kosher no matter who built it, if its covering is proper
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא, remembered by the memory-word גנבך, teaches that a סוכה made by gentiles, by women, for animals, by כותים, or of any kind is כשרה, as long as its סכך is done properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rabbis taught, with the memory-word גנבך: a סוכה of gentiles, a סוכה of women, a סוכה of animals, a סוכה of כותים, a סוכה of any kind is כשרה, provided it is covered properly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא. It lists different booths and says all of them are valid as a סוכה, as long as the covering is made correctly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Who built the booth does not matter, and neither does what it was built for. Even gentiles, or someone building a shed for animals, can produce a kosher סוכה. The only requirement is that the סכך meets the halachic standard. The word גנבך is just a memory aid made from the first letters: גוים, נשים, בהמה, כותים.

keyTerms.meaning: memory-word made from the first letters of גוים, נשים, בהמה, כותים
covered with סכך according to its law

steps.confusionAlert: A סוכה of women does not mean women are obligated in the מצוה. It only means a booth that women built or use is still valid for a man to fulfill the מצוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the halachic principle that the builder or the original purpose does not disqualify a סוכה. Only the physical standard of the סכך matters.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: (mnemonic) G-N-B-K:
a booth of gentiles, a booth of women,
a booth of animals, a booth of Samaritans,
a booth of any sort, is valid,
provided that it is roofed according to its law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New ברייתא. It moves from potters' booths to the general rule that the builder or the purpose does not disqualify a סוכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any booth, whoever built it and for whatever purpose, is a כשרה סוכה if its סכך is made properly.

steps.title: What does 'properly' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word כהלכתה ('properly') means in the גנב״ך ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the last word of the ברייתא from step 6 and asks what it means. This sets up רב חסדא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said all these unusual סוכות are כשרה 'as long as the סכך is done properly.' The גמרא wants to know what 'properly' adds. The basic rules of סכך are already known, so the word must be teaching something extra.

phrases.english: What is 'properly'?
phrases.notes: Refers to the end of the גנב״ך ברייתא (step 6).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a word in the ברייתא quoted in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the condition כהלכתה in the גנב״ך ברייתא.

steps.title: רב חסדא: it must be made for shade
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that 'properly' means the סוכה was built to give shade.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: and that is, provided he made it for the shade of a סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question: 'properly' means the booth was made so that its roof gives shade.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Booths made by gentiles, women, or for animals were not built for the מצוה. So you might think they need nothing special. רב חסדא says the roof still has to be made to give shade (צל), and not just for privacy or storage. If it was, the סוכה is כשרה even though it was not built for סוכות.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, a Sage of the גמרא
For the shade of a סוכה, built so the roof gives shade

steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא does NOT require that the booth be built for the מצוה of סוכה. It only has to be built to give shade. That is why a booth made by a gentile or for animals can still be כשרה.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
And that is provided he made it for the shade of a sukka.
phrases.notes: The roof must be meant to give shade.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: וְהוּא שֶׁעֲשָׂאָהּ לְצֵל סוּכָּה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: כהלכתה means the booth was made to provide shade (לצל סוכה).
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule for any booth not built for the מצוה: it is כשרה if its roof was meant for shade.

steps.title: What does 'any kind' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the phrase 'a סוכה of any kind' comes to include.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks at the last item in the גנב״ך list, 'a סוכה of any kind,' and asks what extra cases it adds. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא already listed four specific kinds of booths: גוים, נשים, בהמה, כותים. Then it added a general phrase, מכל מקום. A general phrase after a list is assumed to add more cases, so the גמרא asks which ones.

keyTerms.meaning: Of any kind, in any case
To include, to bring in more cases

phrases.english: 'Of any kind' comes to include what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a second phrase in the same ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra booths the general phrase מכל מקום includes.

steps.title: It includes the רקב״ש booths
steps.stepSummary: The answer: 'any kind' includes the booths in the list remembered as רקב״ש.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include the סוכה of רקב״ש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'any kind' brings in another group of booths, remembered by the memory-word רקב״ש. It will quote that list next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רקב״ש is a memory code, like גנב״ך. Each letter stands for one type of booth. The point is that these booths count too.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory-word: רועים, קייצים, בורגנין, שומרי פירות
A memory sign used to remember a list

phrases.english: To include: the booth of reish-kuf-beit-shin.
phrases.notes: The letters are spelled out in the next step.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מכל מקום includes the רקב״ש booths.

steps.title: The ברייתא of shepherds' and watchmen's booths
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that booths of shepherds, fig-driers, field guards, produce guards, or of any kind are כשרה if roofed properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Rabbis taught: the סוכה of רקב״ש. The booth of shepherds, the booth of fig-driers, the booth of field guards, the booth of produce guards, a booth of any kind, is כשרה, as long as its roof is done properly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that lists the רקב״ש booths and spells out each letter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are work huts that people put up in the fields for shade while they work. They were not built for סוכות, but the ברייתא says they are כשרה as long as the סכך is proper. This second ברייתא has the same structure as the גנב״ך one, including its own 'any kind' and 'properly.'

keyTerms.meaning: As the Rabbis taught, introducing a ברייתא
Workers who dry figs in summer
Guards of fields, in small watch huts

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
The booth of reish-kuf-beit-shin:
The booth of shepherds, the booth of fig-driers,
the booth of field guards, the booth of produce guards,
a booth of any kind, is fit,
provided that it is roofed properly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source referred to in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Work booths of shepherds, fig-driers, field guards, produce guards, or any booth are כשרה if their סכך is done properly.

steps.title: What does 'properly' mean in this second list?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question about כהלכתה, now in the רקב״ש ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats its earlier question, now about the second ברייתא. This sets up the same answer from רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words are the same as in step 7, but the target is new: the רקב״ש ברייתא. The גמרא checks whether 'properly' means the same thing here.

phrases.english: What is 'properly'?
phrases.notes: Now refers to the רקב״ש ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the step 7 question again, about the newly quoted ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of כהלכתה in the רקב״ש ברייתא.

steps.title: Same answer: made for shade
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא gives the same answer: the booth must be made to give shade.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: and that is, provided he made it for the shade of a סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the same way as before: 'properly' means the booth was built to give shade.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A work hut in a field is made for shade, so it usually passes this test. The rule is the same for both lists: the roof must be meant to give shade.

keyTerms.meaning: The roof covering of a סוכה
And that is, provided that (adds a condition)

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
And that is provided he made it for the shade of a sukka.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: וְהוּא שֶׁעֲשָׂאָהּ לְצֵל סוּכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 with the same answer as step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In the רקב״ש ברייתא too, כהלכתה means the booth was made for shade.

steps.title: What does 'any kind' add in this second list?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'any kind' includes in the רקב״ש ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the general phrase at the end of the second list adds. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רקב״ש list also ends with 'a סוכה of any kind.' Since the first list's 'any kind' pointed to this second list, we now ask where the second one points.

keyTerms.meaning: An inclusion, a phrase that adds more cases

phrases.english: 'Of any kind' comes to include what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the step 9 question again, about the רקב״ש ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the מכל מקום of the רקב״ש ברייתא includes.

steps.title: It includes the גנב״ך booths
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the 'any kind' of the רקב״ש list includes the גנב״ך list. Each list includes the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include the סוכה of גנב״ך.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the second list's 'any kind' brings in the first list, גנב״ך. So the two lists point to each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each ברייתא lists one group by name and uses מכל מקום to include the other group. Together they show that a סוכה is judged by its roof and its purpose of shade. Who built it and why does not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: Memory-word: גוים, נשים, בהמה, כותים (the step 6 list)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two lists of booths not built for the מצוה: גנב״ך (gentiles, women, animals, כותים) and רקב״ש (shepherds, fig-driers, field guards, produce guards). All are כשרה if the roof was made for shade (רב חסדא). Each list's 'any kind' includes the other list.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a circular argument. It just means that each ברייתא names one group openly and includes the other group through the phrase 'any kind.'

phrases.english: To include: the booth of gimmel-nun-beit-kaf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 and closes the comparison of the two ברייתות.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מכל מקום of the רקב״ש ברייתא includes the גנב״ך booths.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both lists are fully included, each through the other's מכל מקום. Any booth whose roof was made for shade is a כשרה סוכה.

steps.title: Why the first תנא names the גנב״ך booths outright
steps.stepSummary: The גנב״ך תנא names those booths outright because they are permanent, so they seem more obviously כשר to him. He uses 'any kind' to add the רקב״ש booths, which are not permanent.
steps.simpleTranslation: This תנא who listed גנב״ך: the גנב״ך booths seem stronger to him because they are permanent. And he taught 'any kind' to include רקב״ש, which are not permanent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the first ברייתא named the גנב״ך booths and left the רקב״ש booths to be included by 'any kind'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said each list includes the other, which raises a question: why does each תנא spell out a different list? Here is the answer for the first תנא. He sees permanence (קביעות) as the stronger reason for a booth to be כשר. So he names the permanent גנב״ך booths outright and uses 'any kind' to add the temporary רקב״ש booths.

keyTerms.meaning: The early teacher (from the time of the משנה) who taught this ברייתא
It is stronger to him: this case seems more obviously valid in his eyes
'Any kind': an extra phrase in the ברייתא that adds more cases
To include, to bring in an additional case

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this תנא holds that the רקב״ש booths are less כשר. Both groups are fully כשר. The only question is which group he names outright and which group he adds through 'any kind'.

phrases.english: This tanna who listed the gimmel-nun-beit-kaf booths,
phrases.notes: גנב״ך: booths of a גוי, women (נשים), animals (בהמה), and כותים.

phrases.english: the gimmel-nun-beit-kaf booths are stronger in his eyes
because they are permanent structures,
phrases.notes: These booths stand all year long, so they look like real dwellings.

phrases.english: and he teaches 'of any kind'
to include the reish-kuf-beit-shin booths, which are not permanent.
phrases.notes: רקב״ש: booths of shepherds, fig-driers, field guards, and produce guards. These are seasonal booths.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי תַּנָּא דְּגַנְבַּ״‎ךְ, אַלִּימָא לֵיהּ גַּנְבַּ״‎ךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind step 15's claim that each list includes the other, starting with the גנב״ך ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The גנב״ך תנא names permanent booths outright and uses 'any kind' to add the temporary רקב״ש booths.

steps.title: Why the second תנא names the רקב״ש booths outright
steps.stepSummary: The רקב״ש תנא names those booths outright because their builders are obligated in סוכה. He uses 'any kind' to add the גנב״ך booths, whose builders are not obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this תנא who listed רקב״ש: the רקב״ש booths seem stronger to him because their builders are obligated in the מצוה. And he taught 'any kind' to include גנב״ך, whose builders are not obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the mirror-image explanation for the second ברייתא, which completes the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second תנא looks at a different factor: whether the builder is obligated in the מצוה (בני חיובא). Shepherds and guards are Jewish men, so they are obligated, and he names their booths outright. גוים, women, and כותים are not obligated, and animals obviously are not, so he adds those booths through 'any kind'.

keyTerms.meaning: People who are obligated in a מצוה, here the מצוה of סוכה

steps.whatToRemember: Both lists are fully כשר according to both ברייתות. Each תנא names outright the group that seems more obviously כשר to him: one because the booths are permanent (קביעות), the other because the builders are obligated (חיוב). The other group comes in through 'any kind'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that two factors could make a booth seem more obviously כשר: how permanent the structure is, and who built it. The halacha ignores both, as long as the booth is roofed properly to give shade.

phrases.english: And this tanna who listed the reish-kuf-beit-shin booths,
the reish-kuf-beit-shin booths are stronger in his eyes
because their builders are people obligated in the מצוה,
and he taught 'of any kind'

phrases.aramaic: לְאֵתוֹיֵי גַּנְבַּ״‎ךְ, דְּלָאו בְּנֵי חִיּוּבָא נִינְהוּ.
phrases.english: to include the gimmel-nun-beit-kaf booths, whose builders are not obligated.
phrases.notes: גוים, women, and כותים are not obligated in סוכה, and a booth made for animals serves occupants who are obviously not obligated.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Each ברייתא names the booths that seem more obviously כשר from its own angle, permanence or obligation, and includes the other list through 'any kind'. All of these booths are כשר if roofed properly.
